sample_unit: microbiologically confirmed infectious keratitis and conjunctivitis cases

links.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy on real clinical cases by input modality versus corneal specialists
links.effect: Image-only accuracy was lowest (best GPT-5, 61.4%; κ=0.38); text-only GPT-5 83.3% vs specialists 87-90%; treatment accuracy 81-85% vs 90-98%.
links.quote: Treatment accuracy remained lower (81-85% vs 90-98%), while urgency triage matched experts in multimodal input.

links.outcome: Multimodal LLM diagnosis, treatment and triage compared with corneal specialists on same cases
links.effect: Image+text near-human accuracy (Perplexity 96.7%; GPT-5 91.7%) without consistently surpassing specialists; text-only and image-only were below specialists; treatment accuracy lower.
links.quote: Combined image+text achieved near-human accuracy without consistently surpassing corneal specialists (Perplexity 96.7%; κ=0.95; GPT-5 91.7%; κ=0.87).

links.outcome: Performance variation across input conditions (image-only, text-only, image+text) and hallucinations
links.effect: Performance depended strongly on input modality; image-only was worst with frequent fungal and Acanthamoeba misclassification and hallucinations confined to the image-only setting.
links.quote: Image-only accuracy was lowest (best GPT-5, 61.4%; κ=0.38) with frequent misclassification of fungal and Acanthamoeba keratitis and hallucinations confined to this setting.

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the performance of multiple commercial multimodal LLMs on retrospective clinical vignettes with slit-lamp photographs against corneal specialists, evaluating diagnostic and triage accuracy without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
